title: What The Socket Says
description: A live tracking-update pushed over the WebSocket is only trustworthy if it actually reflects what got written to the database in that same instant — not a stale snapshot or an optimistic guess.
successCondition: Connect to GET /api/tracking/ws?token=<accessToken> for a shipment you can see. Call POST /api/tracking/:id/advance and capture the resulting { "type": "tracking-update", "shipment": {...} } message's status/currentLat/currentLng/positionUpdatedAt. Immediately querying the shipments table via `npm run db:psql` for that row confirms every one of those fields exactly matches what the WebSocket broadcast, field for field — the push isn't racing ahead of or lagging behind the actual commit.
hints: The broadcast happens after the Prisma update completes inside the same request handler (apps/api/src/modules/tracking/service.ts /routes.ts), so the two should never disagree — this challenge is about proving that, not assuming it.
positionUpdatedAt in the WebSocket payload is ISO-formatted JSON; compare it against Postgres's position_updated_at down to the same instant, allowing only for serialization format differences.
